rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes SPS of single-phase ZrB2 at ~1900 °C, while the target uses SPS of a ZrB2-AlFeNiCoCr cermet at 1300–1600 °C. These are different kinds of intervention (single-phase ceramic vs. cermet with a high-entropy-alloy binder).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies SPS under vacuum/inert atmosphere at ~1900 °C and testing in a molten salt bath at ~900 °C. The target uses SPS under vacuum at 1300–1600 °C and tests in molten Al at 700 °C. The processing and service environments differ in temperature and medium.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes reduced porosity and finer microstructure via SPS to limit liquid ingress. The target's mechanism relies on a liquid HEA binder filling pores and bonding grains at an optimal temperature, with corrosion resistance tied to binder distribution and phase reactions. These are different mechanistic classes.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts lower porosity and improved integrity in a molten salt bath. The target predicts and measures optimal density, hardness, toughness, and molten-Al corrosion/wear resistance for a specific sintering temperature. The predicted property (integrity in a plating bath) differs from the measured properties (density, hardness, toughness, Al corrosion rate, wear volume).
